title: Deep M5.5+ earthquake pairs within 200 km had a seven-day excess under regional time shuffles in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether deep earthquakes formed close pairs more often than expected after regional event times were held fixed. We used 785 events deeper than 300 km in a fixed global ComCat M5.5+ snapshot for 2000-2025. We counted 175 unordered pairs within 200 km Earth chord distance and seven days in the same year. Times were shuffled among locations within each year and 20-degree geographic cell. In 9,999 draws, the mean was 130.21 pairs and the central 95% range was 114-148. The upper-tail Monte Carlo p-value was 0.0001. This tests fine spatial concentration during regional activity. It does not estimate a causal triggering rate. Grid choice, sparse events, mixed magnitude scales, location errors and the exchangeability assumption limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent scalar audit. External event records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Observed deep pair counts and conditional permutation reference counts. The intervals are null ranges, not effect confidence intervals.
